Title: Singh-Gau ki Katha
Notes: No full text online; the best free source is the verse extract and discussion in Padam's Darbari Ratan (1976), pp. 88–91.

Title: Rajniti Ra Kabit (also Rajniti)
Notes: Only specimen stanzas are available, in Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 88–91); no edition or manuscript scan found online.

Title: Lav Kus di Var
Authors: Pandit Devi Das (Padam; Encyclopaedia of Sikhism); listed only as 'attributed' on bhainandlal.com
Notes: Get Padam's Punjabi Varan (archive.org copy), which prints the full var; Darbari Ratan only refers to it.

Title: Hitopadesa (Hindi verse translation)
Notes: No scan of the Braj text online; use Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 92–95) for extracts and GRETIL for the Sanskrit original. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Rajniti Granth
Authors: Tansukh Lahori (re-versification); based on Lakhan Rai's Hitopadesha translation sent from Anandpur
Notes: No edition online; Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 96–100) gives extracts, and GRETIL has the Sanskrit Hitopadesha. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Chanakya Niti
Notes: Only extracts are available (Padam, Darbari Ratan pp. 103–104); the Sanskrit Chanakya Niti is on sanskritdocuments.org. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Sri Gur Sobha
Notes: Start with the 1925 Akali Kaur Singh print and the Ganda Singh (1967) critical edition; use Shah or Kulwant Singh for English.

Title: Karkhe Patshah Dasvin Ke (Kadkhe Patshah Dasvin Ke)
Authors: Sainapati (Padam; the book); poet signing 'Sain' — identification with Sainapati is made by some scholars only
Notes: Best source is the full text in Padam's Punjabi Varan; Darbari Ratan has the discussion. No manuscript scan found.

Title: Pandava Gita
Notes: Only the extract in Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 108–109) is online; a Gurmukhi 'Pandava Gita' manuscript on archive.org (pandav_gtia) is a different prose text. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Kanak Manjri
Notes: Nothing downloadable; the only lead is Padam's note that the manuscript is at Guler, Kangra (Darbari Ratan p. 109).

Title: Parsuram Sanvad
Notes: Read the kabitts in a Gurmukhi Hanuman Natak (1899 print on archive.org) and Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 111–113). saved file is Hirde Ram's Hanuman Natak (Parashurama episode), not Kashi Ram's work

Title: Sabha Parab
Notes: Only extracts in Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 123–128) are online; the sole manuscript is in the Patiala royal collection. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Poetry in various meters
Notes: Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 123–128) is the only free source for his miscellaneous verse; a stanza is also quoted in Santokh Singh's Suraj Granth (ritu 5, ansu 26).

Title: Salya Parva (Shalya Parab)
Notes: Only colophon and extracts in Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 129–133); the manuscript in Patiala is not digitised online. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Petitions addressing Mata Jito
Notes: The petition's text is printed in Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 129–130); its manuscript source (an old Dasam Granth copy) is not identified online.

Title: Kabitts (Punjabi and Hindi)
Notes: Padam's Darbari Ratan (pp. 129–133) is the only free collection of Mangal's verse found.

Title: 50 Upanishads (Bhakha translation); MS titled 'Upanishad Atharvan Bhakha'
Notes: Prahlad's own text survives only in a Patiala manuscript; read extracts in Darbari Ratan (pp. 115–122) and his Persian source, the Sirr-i Akbar.

Title: Sikhan di Bhagatmala (Sikkhan di Bhagat-mal)
Authors: Bhai Mani Singh (d. 1734; traditional); Giani Surat Singh of the Gianian Bunga, from Mani Singh's oral teaching (Padam); unnamed author (most modern scholars). Note: no source found that separates two different Mani Singhs; worth checking in print
Notes: Get the old Gurmukhi manuscript scans plus Bhai Vir Singh's 1912 edition; Padam's 2013 critical edition is a paid Singh Brothers book.

Title: Gyan Ratanavali (Mani Singh Janam Sakhi)
Authors: Bhai Mani Singh (traditional); Giani Surat Singh (Padam and others); an Udasi writer, early 19th c. (Surjit Hans). Note: the text refers to Mani Singh in the third person
Notes: Best free copy is the 1890 Lahore lithograph on archive.org; Kirpal Singh (1969) provides an abridged scholarly text.

Title: Diwan-i-Goya
Notes: Get Ganda Singh's Persian-script Kulliyat (1963) or Tasnifat-e-Goya for the original, and his Granthavali for a Gurmukhi version with translation.

Title: Zindaginama (Bandginama)
Notes: Get the Persian text in Ganda Singh's Kulliyat or Tasnifat-e-Goya and the Gurmukhi version with translation in his Granthavali; no manuscript scan found.

Title: Ganjnama
Notes: Get the Persian text from Ganda Singh's Kulliyat or Tasnifat-e-Goya and Bhai Vir Singh's 1914 steek for a classic commentary.

Title: Tausif-o-Sana
Notes: Available in Ganda Singh's Persian-script Kulliyat or Tasnifat-e-Goya and in his Gurmukhi Granthavali (p. 210); no separate edition found.

Title: Joti Bigas (Persian)
Notes: Get the Persian text from Ganda Singh's Kulliyat or Tasnifat-e-Goya and the Gurmukhi version with translation in his Granthavali (p. 162).

Title: Dastur-ul-Insha
Notes: Only the surviving fragment is available, printed in Ganda Singh's Granthavali (p. 194) and Nangli's Granthavali (p. 336); Nangli says the full manuscript, once seen in the family, is now rare.

Title: Arz ul-Alfaz
Notes: Get Ganda Singh's 1963 Persian Kulliyat for the original text and his Punjabi University Granthavali for a Gurmukhi transliteration with translation, both free on archive.org; no manuscript scan was found.

Title: Joti Bigas (Punjabi/Bhakha version)
Notes: Best source is Ganda Singh's Granthavali (free scan, two hosts), with Bindra's Kalaam-e-Goya for English; no manuscript scan of the Gurmukhi Joti Bigas was found online.

Title: Prashan Uttar (Rahitnama Bhai Nand Lal)
Authors: Bhai Nand Lal Goya (traditional; the book); an early copy circulates untitled as 'Nasihatnama' (GNDU MS 440, c. 1718–19, per G.S. Mann)
Notes: For a usable text get Ganda Singh's Granthavali or Padam's Rahitname, with Bindra for English; no early manuscript (e.g. GNDU MS 440) is digitised online.

Title: Sakhi Rahit Ki
Authors: Bhai Nand Lal (the book; bhainandlal.com); anonymous, mid-1730s (McLeod's material names no author)
Notes: Padam's Rahitname (free scan) is the only downloadable edition found; for context use McLeod and Malhotra. No manuscript scan was found.

Title: Rahitnama Chaupa Singh (Hazuri Rahitnama)
Authors: Bhai Chaupa Singh (d. 1724; family tradition, Padam); composite text compiled from several sources c. 1740–65 (McLeod)
Notes: McLeod's 1987 critical edition and translation is the best version and is free on archive.org; Padam's Rahitname has the Punjabi text. No manuscript scan was found.

Title: Love poetry in various ragas
Notes: No standalone edition or manuscript scan exists online; Padam's Darbari Ratan (free) is the best source for Nanua's raga poems.

Title: Panj Sau Sakhi (Sau Sakhi)
Authors: Bhai Ram Kuir / Ram Kanwar, later Gurbakhsh Singh (traditional narrator), written down by Sahib Singh; Gurbux Singh Raindar (some); later interpolators (text surfaced only in 1815)
Notes: Get the PDL-digitised 19th-century manuscript and Attar Singh's 1873 English Sakhee Book, then Padam's edited text; note that the work's date and authenticity are disputed.

Title: Karna Parva (Karan Parab)
Notes: The Braj Karan Parab exists only in the Patiala manuscript; read the extracts in Padam's Darbari Ratan, with the Sanskrit (GRETIL/BORI) and Roy translation for comparison. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Various poetry
Notes: No separate collection exists; Padam's Darbari Ratan and Bharat Bhushan's study (both free on archive.org) hold the only published samples.

Title: Drona Parva (Dron Parab)
Notes: Kunvresh's Dron Parab survives only as an unpublished fragment; Padam's Darbari Ratan has extracts, with the Sanskrit and Ganguli translation for comparison. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Samudrik
Notes: No edition or scan of Kunvresh's Samudrik exists; Padam's Darbari Ratan is the only published source, citing an Anandpur manuscript of 1696. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Rati Rahasya Kos
Notes: No edition or scan of Kunvresh's text exists; Padam's Darbari Ratan has the only extracts. Kokkoka's Sanskrit Ratirahasya is available for comparison. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Asvamedha Parva
Notes: No edition or scan exists; use Padam's extracts, plus the Sanskrit (GRETIL/BORI) and Ganguli for comparison. The 1696 Anandpur copy is known only from catalogues. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Ratan Dam (Amar Kosh Bhakha)
Notes: Tahkan's Ratan Dam is unpublished (Patiala MS); Padam's Darbari Ratan has extracts, and the Sanskrit Amarakosha is on GRETIL.

Title: Futkal Chands
Notes: No separate edition exists; Padam's Darbari Ratan (free) prints Tahkan's miscellaneous chhands.

Title: Poetry in various ragas
Notes: No standalone edition exists; Padam's Darbari Ratan has Tahkan's raga poems (Tilang, Bilaval) and is free on archive.org.

Title: Karna Parva
Notes: Chand's Karan Parab is lost; only his own mention of it survives, quoted in Padam's Darbari Ratan. For the content, see the Sanskrit and the Roy translation. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Udyoga Parva (Udyog Parab)
Notes: Chand's Udyog Parab survives only in the Patiala manuscript; Padam's Darbari Ratan has extracts, and the Sanskrit and the 1886 translation give the content. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Parichha
Notes: No scan or edition exists; the work is known from Patiala Bhasha Vibhag MS 135 and Padam's listing.

Title: Triya Charitra
Authors: Chand (pen-name in the manuscript; Padam; the book); relation to the Dasam Granth Charitropakhyan unclear — that text's own authorship is debated (Guru Gobind Singh / court poets)
Notes: No copy of Chand's own Triya Charitra is online; Padam names it, and the Dasam Granth Charitropakhyan (separate, disputed authorship) is available in 19th-century manuscripts and prints.

Title: Poetry about the Gurus; various other poetry
Notes: Padam's Darbari Ratan (free) has the collected miscellaneous verse; no other edition exists.

Title: Jangnama Guru Gobind Singh Ji Ka
Notes: Get Ashok's Prachin Varan te Jangname (1950, free PDL scan) for the Gurmukhi text, with Goyal's 1971 Devanagari edition as a second version.

Title: Adhyatam Prakash
Authors: Sukhdev (Sukhdev Mishra, Kanyakubja Brahman, b. Kapilnagar)
Notes: Best versions are the 1857 Gurmukhi manuscript and the 1932 Devanagari print, both free on archive.org; Randhawa's steek gives the Sikh teaching commentary.

Title: Chhand Vichar Pingal
Notes: No edition or scan is online; the text is known from a Khalsa College manuscript, with discussion in Padam and Bharat Bhushan.

Title: Vrind Satsai (Vrinda Satasai)
Notes: Two Gurmukhi manuscripts (Kurukshetra, Panjab University) and the 1971 Vrind Granthavali are all free on archive.org.

Title: Bhav Panchashika (Bhava Panchasika)
Notes: Get the 1971 Vrind Granthavali (free DLI scan) for the full text; Padam's Darbari Ratan supplies the Anandpur link and the Patiala Gurmukhi MS 201 lead, which is not digitised.

Title: Shringar Shiksha
Notes: The 1971 Vrind Granthavali (free DLI scan) is the only accessible text; no Gurmukhi copy of this work was found online.

Title: Hitopadesh Natak (per Wikipedia)
Notes: Use the Hitopadeshashtak in the 1971 Vrind Granthavali; that it is the book's 'Hitupdesha Shatak' is likely but not certain, and the Sanskrit Hitopadesha is on GRETIL.

Title: Pavath Pachisi
Notes: Pavath Pachisi is almost certainly Vrind's Pavan Pachisi, printed for the first time in the 1971 Vrind Granthavali (free DLI scan).

Title: Yamkalankar
Notes: Treat Yamkalankar as Vrind's Yamak Satsai (a probable identification), available in the 1971 Vrind Granthavali; no separate Gurmukhi copy was found.

Title: Pingal Sar
Notes: There is no edition: Padam's Darbari Ratan extracts (free) are the only readable text, and the full work survives in Patiala and Agra manuscripts known only from catalogues.

Title: Stanza praising the Guru's generosity; also Shyam Sanehi, Sudama Charitar, Alim Keli (1696)
Other titles: Poetry about the Guru in different meters
Notes: Padam's Darbari Ratan (free archive.org scan) is where to get the actual poems in the meters and ragas named; no manuscript scan was found.

Title: Kharkha Guru Gobind Singh Ka
Notes: Darbari Ratan has the complete text; the source manuscript is known only from the SRL catalogue.

Title: Various poems about love
Notes: Only one stanza survives in print, in Darbari Ratan (free); no other love poems by Nand Ram were found.

Title: Prem Ambodh Pothi (Prem Abodh)
Authors: Hari Das (Padam; the book); Kevaldas (R.S. Jaggi); Guru Gobind Singh (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism; SikhiWiki); unknown (Hawley & Mann)
Notes: Best set: the illustrated Gurmukhi MS and Usahan's 1989 Punjabi University edition, both free on archive.org, with Hawley & Mann's JPS article for the manuscript history and authorship.

Title: Panchatantra (Braj/Panjabi rendering)
Notes: No Anandpur-period Braj or Gurmukhi Panchatantra by Dharam Singh survives online (Padam reports the family copy was lost); the free Sanskrit text and Edgerton's 1930 critical text are the best substitutes. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Kok Sanvad
Notes: Only Padam's description and opening savaiya are online; the book's 'MS 3, private collection' remains the sole known copy.

Title: Katha Raje Bharthari Hari Ki
Notes: No edition or scan exists online; the lead is Moti Bagh Library, Patiala, MS 139, recorded in Darbari Ratan.

Title: Vaar Sri Bhagauti Ji Ki Patshahi Dasvin Ki (41st Var)
Authors: Bhai Gurdas Singh ('Gurdas II'), Kavi Darbar poet, brother of Alam Singh Nachna (the book; Wikipedia); a later 18th-c. Gurdas, c. mid-1780s (McLeod; dating by Fenech & Vir Singh); Bhai Gurdas Bhalla (d. 1636) by manuscript title 'Vaar Bhai Gurdas Ji Ki' and its placement as the 41st Var — though its 1699 subject postdates him; separately, an anonymous 'Var Patshahi Dasvin Ki' on the Nirmohgarh battle (published by Padam, 1967)
Notes: Padam ties this title to Var 41 (Gurdas Singh's Var on the Khalsa), so get the 19th-c. manuscript pothis and the Randhawa steek; whether it dates to Anandpur is disputed.

Title: Barahmaha Sri Ram Chandar
Authors: Bhai Gurdas Singh ('Gurdas II') (the book; Wikipedia) — said to be written soon after 1708; not Bhai Gurdas Bhalla
Notes: Get the full text from Padam's Punjabi Baramahe (1959, free on archive.org); the post-1708 date some scholars give puts it outside the Anandpur period.

Title: Pryaye Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji / Sri Guru Granth Prayay
Other titles: Praya Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji Ke
Authors: Bhai Gurdas Singh ('Gurdas II') (the book; Wikipedia citing 'Sri Dasam Granth: Facts Beyond Doubt', 2021); anonymous, late 18th/early 19th c. (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, for 'Sri Guru Granth Prayay')
Notes: Nothing downloadable: the only known copy is Khalsa College, Amritsar, MS 1473 (catalogue free on archive.org), and whether it is Gurdas Singh's work is uncertain.

Title: Poetry in various ragas
Notes: Darbari Ratan (free) has exactly the four raga poems listed; no other source was found.

Title: Gur Mahima
Notes: The 'Gur Mahima' verses survive only as the four kabitts in Darbari Ratan (free download).

Title: Warrior poetry challenging the enemies
Notes: Darbari Ratan (free) contains the full set of kabitts, savaiya and chhappay the book describes.

Title: Poetry praising Guru Gobind Singh
Notes: Only Padam's Darbari Ratan (free) preserves Sundar's three kabitts.

Title: Poetry praising Guru Gobind Singh
Notes: Only Padam's Darbari Ratan (free) preserves Sharda's two kabitts.

Title: Poetry praising Guru Gobind Singh
Notes: One kabitt survives, in Darbari Ratan (free download).

Title: Mystical poetry; poem praising Guru Nanak's rabab
Notes: Only a few mystical lines (Darbari Ratan, free) are available; the rabab poem was not located.

Title: Various poetry
Notes: Darbari Ratan (free) has Chandan's two surviving poems.

Title: Various poetry
Notes: Darbari Ratan (free) has Dhanna Singh's savaiya; nothing else was found.

Title: Various poetry
Notes: The only text located is Padam's Darbari Ratan (1976), p. 208, which prints Ramdas's single surviving kafi; the scan is free on archive.org.

Title: Poetry in Sanskrit
Notes: Get Darbari Ratan p. 209, which quotes Brij Lal's Sanskrit shloka. The underlying source is Suraj Granth Rut 5 Ansu 27, and a Gurmukhi Suraj Granth PDF is free on archive.org. saved file is Santokh Singh's Suraj Granth, not Brij Lal's own Sanskrit verse

Title: Pauṛīāṅ Gurū Gobind Siṅgh Kīāṅ (Pauri Guru Gobind Singh Ki)
Other titles: Poetry on the battle of Bhangani
Notes: Darbari Ratan pp. 210–211 (free on archive.org) prints Chhabila's Bhangani pauris. Ashok's printed editions (1951, 1971) were not found online.

Title: Pauṛīāṅ Gurū Gobind Siṅgh Kīāṅ (Mushki's portion)
Notes: Darbari Ratan p. 211 (free on archive.org) gives Mir Mushki's surviving karkha, confirming the 'kharkha meter' attribution.

Title: Poetry in praise of a friend soon to be married
Notes: Darbari Ratan p. 214 (free on archive.org) prints Desa Singh Bhatt's wedding pauris. Padam's source, Garja Singh's Shahid Bilas, is also on archive.org. saved file is Kavi Sewa Singh's Shahid Bilas, not Desa Singh Bhatt's poem

Title: Srī Gurū Granth Prayāy (similar title)
Authors: Bhai Kirat Singh (the book, via Padam); anonymous (Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, for 'Sri Guru Granth Prayay'); later paryai compilers, e.g. Chanda Singh (1848)
Notes: Darbari Ratan p. 216 (free) confirms Padam's attribution of a Guru Granth Prayay to Kirat Singh. No full text is online; the nearest manuscript lead is Khalsa College MS 1473.

Title: Jhagra Heer Ranjhe Ka
Notes: Darbari Ratan p. 218 (free on archive.org) confirms Kallua's Jhagra Heer Ranjhe Ka (10 kabits). No separate manuscript or edition was found online.

Title: Poetry about his love for the Guru
Notes: The only text found is Darbari Ratan p. 224 (free on archive.org), which prints Maha Singh's surviving devotional verse.

Title: Bāz-nāma
Notes: No Anandpur Baznama survives online. Padam's EoS entry attests that hawk manuals were made at the court; Persian Baz-nama texts on archive.org are the nearest comparisons. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Filnama
Notes: No Anandpur Filnama was found. The court's animal manuals are attested only through Padam's EoS entry; Sanskrit elephant treatises are offered for comparison. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Aspnama
Notes: No Anandpur Aspnama was found. Persian Faras-nama texts (Phillott 1910, free) are the closest available parallels. Saved: the source text, not the Anandpur rendering

Title: Suan Nama (ਸੁਆਨ ਨਾਮਾ)
Notes: No digitised copy. Only known MS: Moti Bagh (Patiala royal) library, per Padam 1976.

Title: Hanuman Natak
Authors: Anonymous (Padam 2000; the book); Hirday Ram Bhalla, c. 1620s (Braj Hanuman Natak); Sanskrit original (Mahanataka) traditionally ascribed to Damodara Mishra
Notes: Best options are the two Gurmukhi manuscript scans on archive.org (PDL pothi; 2-volume illuminated MS), then the 1883 Gurmukhi lithograph. The work is by Hirday Ram Bhalla, not anonymous.

Title: Sur Sagar
Authors: Anonymous (Padam 2000; the book); Surdas (the standard Sur Sagar)
Notes: Get the Panjab University Braj manuscript (MS 823) and the 1907 Khemraj print. The author is Surdas, not anonymous, and no Gurmukhi/Anandpur copy is online.

Title: Sar Gita (ਸਾਰ ਗੀਤਾ)
Notes: Sar Gita: anonymous Bhakha prose; Gurmukhi MS (UPSS 4151) and Devanagari MS (Jammu 957-gha) saved, plus the Sanskrit source.

Title: Pothi Salihotar Ki
Authors: Muhammad Akbar (Padam 2000; the book); not matched to the known works of the physician Muhammad Akbar Arzani
Notes: The Muhammad Akbar text itself was not found. The best related download is the Gurmukhi Shalihotra manuscript (Kurukshetra Univ. MN-000049) on archive.org. saved file is a general Shalihotra (horse-medicine) MS, not Muhammad Akbar's pothi

Title: Pothi Vaidgi Ki
Authors: Muhammad Akbar (Padam 2000; the book); not matched to the known works of the physician Muhammad Akbar Arzani
Notes: No 'Pothi Vaidgi Ki' was found. A Gurmukhi Vaidyak Granth manuscript (Panjab Univ. MS 354) on archive.org is the nearest genre example. saved file is a general Vaidyak Granth MS, not Muhammad Akbar's pothi

Title: Mujarrabāt-i Akbarī
Notes: Two free downloads: a Persian Mujarrabat-i Akbari manuscript (DLI) and an 1892 Gurmukhi-script translation. Neither is confirmed as the copy known at Anandpur, and the Arzani attribution is unconfirmed.

Title: Shāhnāma
Notes: Get Macan's 1829 Calcutta Persian text and Warner's translation (both free). The Anandpur link runs through the Zafarnama (Padam ed. free; Fenech 2013 paid), and no Anandpur-era Shahnama copy is known online.

Title: Gulistān
Notes: Get the Sprenger 1851 Persian text and Eastwick's translation (both free). The Anandpur connection is shown through the Zafarnama, and no Anandpur-era copy is known.

Title: Būstān
Notes: A Persian Bostan manuscript (DLI, vol. 2), the 1877 Persian print and Clarke's translation are all free. The Anandpur connection runs through the Zafarnama.

Title: Hitopadesha
Notes: Best is the Panjab University Gurmukhi manuscript of Tansukh's Rajniti (MS 423), with Darbari Ratan pp. 92–100 for Lakhan Rai's 1680 Hitopadesh. Lakhan Rai's own manuscript (Bhasha Vibhag Patiala 408) is not online.

Title: Upanishads
Notes: Get the Panjab University Gurmukhi bhakha Upanishad manuscript (MS 422) and Darbari Ratan's Prahilad Rai chapter. GRETIL and Max Müller are the Sanskrit and English references.

Title: Balmiki (Valmiki) Ramayana
Notes: For the Gurmukhi tradition, get the Panjab University Gurmukhi Ramayana MS 118 and Santokh Singh's 1834 Braj Valmiki. GRETIL and Griffith are the Sanskrit and English references; no Anandpur copy is known.

Title: Vashisht (Vasishtha)
Notes: Two Gurmukhi bhakha Yog Vasishtha manuscripts are free on archive.org (Kurukshetra MN-000214; PU MS 46), with the 1937 Sanskrit edition and Mitra's translation as references.

Title: Chanakya (Chanakya Niti / Chanakya Rajniti)
Authors: Sainapati as translator (secondary sources); Twarikh Guru Khalsa names no translator
Notes: Best are the Gurmukhi Chanakyagranth MS (PU 102) and the 1921 Sanskrit Chanakya Rajniti; Sainapati's attributed Anandpur verse version has no known edition or scan.

Title: Guru Gita; Khasat Shastr; (Shastrodip?) Suraj
Notes: Only the Sanskrit Guru Gita can be downloaded; no Anandpur-period Bhasha version of the Guru Gita or the other works merged into this title was found. saved file is a Guru Gita Stotra print; the TGK title itself is unclear

Title: Niti Shakat
Notes: Nothing downloadable: 'Niti Shakat' cannot be identified, so only Gian Singh's Twarikh Guru Khalsa, which names it, is available.

Title: Devi Bhagvat (Devi Bhagavata Purana)
Notes: Get the Khemraj Sanskrit pothi and Vijnanananda's 1922 translation; no Braj or Gurmukhi Devi Bhagavat tied to Anandpur was found.

Title: Bishnu Bhagvat da Dasam [Skandh]
Notes: Best are the Gurmukhi Dasam Skandh MSS (PU 1483, Kurukshetra MN 003222) and the Krishna Avatar in early Dasam Granth birs; the specific Anandpur translation is not identified.

Title: Ikadash Skand (Bhagavata Purana, 11th skandha)
Notes: No Anandpur-period Ikadash Skandh survives online; the Gurmukhi Bhagavata MSS (PU 299, Kurukshetra MN 003300) and Bhasha eleventh-skandh versions are the closest downloads.

Title: Padam Puran (Padma Purana)
Notes: Best are the two Kurukshetra Gurmukhi Padam Puran MSS; for the Sanskrit original, use the 1894 Anandasrama edition.

Title: Visan Puran (Vishnu Purana)
Notes: Get the PU 'Bishan Puran Bhasha' Gurmukhi MS first, then the Kurukshetra Gurmukhi copies; GRETIL and Wilson cover the Sanskrit and English.

Title: Mahabharat
Authors: Various court poets (e.g., Kunvaresh, Drona Parv; Mangal Rai, Shalya Parv; Amrit Rai)
Notes: No court Mahabharata parv is online; use GRETIL/Ganguli for the text and Mann's article plus the EoS entries for the Anandpur renderings.

Title: Jaimini [Ashvamedh]
Notes: Only Sanskrit Jaimini Ashvamedha copies are downloadable (Ramtek MS, 1892 Bombay print); no Braj/Gurmukhi court version was found.

Title: Bhoj Prabandh
Notes: Get the Sharada MS and the 1881-83 prints; no Anandpur or Gurmukhi Bhoj Prabandh was found.

Title: Shukar Niti (Shukraniti)
Notes: Use Oppert's 1882 Sanskrit edition and Sarkar's 1914 translation; no Anandpur Bhasha Shukraniti was found.

Title: Bahar-e Danish
Authors: Inayat Allah Kamboh (Persian original, 1651); Bhasha version made via Bhai Nand Chand per TGK
Notes: Get the DLI Persian MS and the 1849 print; no Gurmukhi/Braj version from Anandpur (via Bhai Nand Chand) survives online.

Title: Manu (Manusmriti)
Notes: Mandlik 1886 or Jolly 1887 for the Sanskrit and Bühler 1886 in English; no Anandpur-period Bhasha Manu was found.

Title: Yagvalak (Yajnavalkya Smriti)
Notes: Stenzler 1849 or the Mitaksara edition for the Sanskrit and Vidyarnava 1918 in English; no Anandpur Bhasha 'Yagvalak' was found.

Title: Rig Veda
Notes: Get the GRETIL text plus Max Müller's Sāyaṇa edition; no Gurmukhi/Braj or Anandpur-linked rendering of the Rig Veda was found.

Title: Sama Veda
Notes: GRETIL text plus Stevenson's 1842–43 text/translation and Griffith 1893; no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Yajur Veda
Notes: Use Wikisource/GRETIL for the Sanskrit and Griffith (White) / Keith (Black) translations; no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Atharva Veda
Notes: GRETIL Śaunaka text plus Whitney's HOS translation; no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Brahma Purana
Notes: GRETIL text and an 1895 printed edition; no Gurmukhi/Braj rendering found (Dasam Granth's 'Brahma Avtar' is a separate composition, not this Purāṇa).

Title: Padma Purana
Notes: Best Sikh-region items are the two Gurmukhi 'Padam Puran' bhākhā manuscripts at Kurukshetra; pair with the 1893 printed Sanskrit text.

Title: Vishnu Purana
Notes: Download the Gurmukhi 'Bishan Puran Bhasha' MS (Panjab Univ. 386) for the Panjabi-tradition rendering, with GRETIL and Wilson for Sanskrit/English.

Title: Shiva Purana
Notes: GRETIL/Wikisource for Sanskrit; no Gurmukhi MS of the Śiva Purāṇa found, the nearest Sikh-tradition text is Dasam Granth's Rudra Avtār.

Title: Bhagwata Purana
Notes: Strongest Sikh link: Dasam Granth's Krishna Avtār (illustrated Gurmukhi MS) plus Gurmukhi Dasham Skandh manuscripts at Kurukshetra and Panjab Univ.; GRETIL for the Sanskrit.

Title: Narayana Purana
Notes: Identity uncertain (probably the Nārada/Nāradīya Purāṇa); GRETIL and the Venkateshwar text are available, no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Markandeya Purana
Notes: Best Sikh-tradition sources are Dasam Granth's Chandī Charitr and Vār Durgā (Patna-bir MS download plus online text); Pargiter and GRETIL cover the Purāṇa itself.

Title: Agni Purana
Notes: GRETIL plus Mitra's 1876 edition and Dutt's translation; no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Bhavishya Purana
Notes: Use Wikisource for the Sanskrit and the 1869/1922 Hindi editions; no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Brahma Vaivarta Purana
Notes: A Panjab-held Sanskrit MS, the 1888 Calcutta text and Sen's 1920 translation; no Gurmukhi rendering found.

Title: Linga Purana
Notes: Panjab Univ. Sanskrit MS, GRETIL text and Jivananda's 1885 edition; no Sikh-tradition rendering found.

Title: Varaha Purana
Notes: Wikisource text and the 1887 Bibliotheca Indica edition; the only Sikh-tradition link is the Barāh Avtār episode in Dasam Granth.

Title: Skanda Purana
Notes: Wikisource for the full Sanskrit, plus GRETIL and the 1877 Sahyādri edition; only a Gurmukhi Kārtik Māhātmya MS touches the Panjabi tradition.

Title: Vamana Purana
Notes: GRETIL and the 1909 Venkateshwar pothi; Dasam Granth's Bāvan Avtār is the only Sikh-tradition link.

Title: Kurma Purana
Notes: GRETIL plus the 1890 Bibliotheca Indica edition; only the Kachh Avtār in Dasam Granth links to the Sikh tradition.

Title: Matsya Purana
Notes: GRETIL, the 1879 text and the SBH translation; Dasam Granth's Machh Avtār is the Sikh-tradition link.

Title: Garuda Purana
Notes: GRETIL plus Dutt's 1908 translation; no Gurmukhi/Sikh-tradition rendering was found online.

Title: Brahmanda Purana
Notes: For the Sikh tradition get Gulab Singh's 1783 Gurmukhi Adhyātam Rāmāyan (Brahmāṇḍa section); GRETIL and a Panjab Univ. MS cover the Purāṇa.

Title: Mahabharata
Notes: The Anandpur Braj parvas survive only in private MSS (catalogue records); download Padam's Darbārī Ratan for excerpts, with GRETIL/Ganguli for the epic.

Title: Ramayana
Notes: Best: Dasam Granth Rām Avtār (Patna-bir MS) and Santokh Singh's 1834 Gurmukhi Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa; GRETIL for the Sanskrit.

Title: Manu Simriti
Notes: GRETIL plus Bühler (free) or Doniger (borrow); no early Gurmukhi/Braj Manusmṛti was found.

Title: Six darshanas: Vedanta, Nyay, Vaisheshik, Sankhya, Yog, Uttar Mimansa
Notes: Gurmukhi Vedānta pothīs (Panjab/Kurukshetra) show the Sikh-region reception; GRETIL has all six sūtra texts, with SBH/SBE translations.

Title: Adhyatam Ramayan (Adhiatam Ramain)
Notes: Best is PU MS 1471 (Gulab Singh, dated 1783), then the illustrated PU MS 1484 and the 1903 Lahore print.

Title: Bachitar Natak (Bachittar Natak)
Authors: Guru Gobind Singh (traditional); contested by some modern scholars (court poets)
Notes: Start with the 1765 Patna Misal and 1777 Kesgarh birs, then Narain Singh's steek; Jodh Singh's 1999 translation is at archive.org/details/the-wondrous-play-bachitra-natak.

Title: Bhasha Bhushan (commentary)
Authors: Harcharandas as commentator (the book); original Bhasha Bhushan by Maharaja Jaswant Singh of Marwar
Notes: Best is PU MS 296, which contains Haricharandas's commentary on Bhasha Bhushan, followed by the 1866 and 1878 prints of the base text.

Title: Ikadas = probably Bhagavat Ekadash Skandh Bhasha (ਇਕਾਦਸ)
Authors: If Chatur Das's Bhagavat Ekadash Skandh Bhasha: Sadhu Chatur Das, disciple of Sant Das (prints of 1926/1927; PU MS 1370); if an Ekadashi-mahatam: e.g. Bal Chand ('Balu Das') of Lahore, court poet (Padam); the book names no author
Notes: Probably Chatur Das's Bhagavat Ekadash Skandh Bhasha (medium confidence); 1926/1927 prints saved; PU MS 1370 is in folder 106. Identity uncertain: probably Chatur Das's Ekadash Skandh Bhasha

Title: Prabodh Chandar Natak (Prabodhachandra Natak)
Notes: Best is the Jammu MS of Gulab Singh's Bhasha version, then the 1894 Lahore Gurmukhi print; the Sanskrit and Taylor editions give the source play.

Title: Tasnif (collected works) of Bhai Nand Lal
Authors: Bhai Nand Lal Goya; Guru Gobind Singh (Zafarnama, Hikayats)
Notes: Get Tasnifat-e-Goya and Ganda Singh's Kulliyat for Nand Lal, plus PU MS 353 and the 1915 Urdu-script Dasam Granth for the Zafarnama/Hikayats; the London MS 3 itself is unscanned.

Title: Ustati Sri Amritsar Ji Ki
Notes: No scan of Saundha's text was found; Dharam Singh's 1981 study is the best download. PU MS 108, Amritsar Ustati by Ram Parkash Udasi, is a different poem.

Title: Uthanka Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji Ki
Authors: Mahant Sadhu Singh of Patiala (arranger, 1898/99 Lahore print); the text's own preface: set down by Bhai Gurdas at Guru Arjan Dev's direction (traditional claim); manuscript cited in the book names no author
Notes: Best is the 1900 Lahore Uthanka print (PDL scan) and Mahant Sadhu Singh's Uthanka; the London manuscript itself is not digitised.

Title: Vaaran Gyan Ratanavali Bhai Gurdas Ji
Gurmukhi: ਵਾਰਾਂ ਗਿਆਨ ਰਤਨਾਵਲੀ ਭਾਈ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ ਜੀ — ਕਠਨ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਆਦਿ ਦੀ ਟਿੱਪਣੀ ਤੇ ਪ੍ਰਯਾਵਾਂ ਸਹਿਤ
Authors: Bhai Gurdas (Bhalla); Vaar 41 by Bhai Gurdas II (Bhai Gurdas Singh)

Title: Vaaran Bhai Gurudas Ji-Bhai Vir Singh Punjabi
Uggardanti
Authors: attributed in the PDF to Guru Gobind Singh (Ugardanti / Bhagauti Chhand, six chhakkas)

Title: Jaap Sahib teeka Chakradhar Charitra Charu Chandrika
Report of the Sodhak Committee on the Dasam Granth
Gurbani Sangeet Prachin Reet Ratnavali
Gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਸੰਗੀਤ ਪ੍ਰਾਚੀਨ ਰੀਤ ਰਤਨਾਵਲੀ (ਭਾਗ ਪਹਿਲਾ) ਅਰਥਾਤ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਰਾਗਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਪੁਰਾਤਨ ਕੀਰਤਨੀ ਰੀਤਾਂ
Authors: Bhai Avtar Singh and Bhai Gurcharan Singh, Hazuri Ragis, Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib, Delhi

Title: Pothi Sri Dasehra Mahatam
Gurmukhi: ਪੋਥੀ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦਸੈਹਰਾ ਮਹਾਤਮ ਅਰਥਾਤ ਸ਼ਸਤ੍ਰ ਪੂਜਾ-ਪਾਠ ਬਿਧੀ
Authors: Guru Gobind Singh (all items are Dasam Granth extracts)

Title: Gur Shabad Sidhi
Gurmukhi: ਗੁਰ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸਿੱਧੀ ਅਰਥਾਤ ਸ਼ਰਧਾ ਪੂਰਨ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ
Authors: Attributed on the title page to 'Sri Man Bhai Mani Singh ji wala' (traditional attribution, unverified)

Title: Nihangnama
Authors: Anthology; excerpts by Rattan Singh Bhangu, Santokh Singh, Giani Gian Singh, Baba Sumer Singh and (attrib.) Bhai Daya Singh

Title: Santan di Mahima
Gurmukhi: ਸੰਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਹਿਮਾਂ — ਕਵੀਸ਼ਰੀ ਕਵਿਤਾਵਾਂ ਦੀ ਪੁਸਤਕ
Authors: Bhai Gurjant Singh Bainka, Hazuri kavishar of the Sampardai Dal Baba Bidhi Chand (kavishri jatha)

Title: Sankhep Bibek
Authors: unknown. The verses carry the chhap 'ਕਹੇ ਜਗਦੀਸ਼ ਹਰੀ', so the verse author may be the same Jagdish named as reviser, but this is unconfirmed

Title: Sri Nanak Prakash Gur Partap Suraj Granth
Braham Kavach
Authors: unknown; the closing dohra reads 'ਇਹ ਬੋਲਾ ਹਰਿਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਕਾ ਸੁਣੋ ਖਾਲਸਾ ਬੀਰ' (attributing it to Guru Hargobind)

Title: Akal Takht hukamnama on Amrit sanchar
Prem Sumarag Granth + Sakhis of the ten Gurus
Complete Steek of Sri Sarbloh Granth Sahib Ji
Gurmukhi: ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਸਟੀਕ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਸਰਬਲੋਹ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ (ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੰਗਲਾ ਚਰਨ ਜੀ) ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੁਖ ਵਾਕ ਪਾ: ੧੦
Authors: Attributed to Guru Gobind Singh (Sri Mukhvak Patshahi 10) as printed

Title: Sri Diwali Path Mahatam – revised/expanded edition
Gurmukhi: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਪਾਠ ਮਹਾਤਮ (ਦੀਪਮਾਲਾ ਅਥਵਾ ਬੰਦੀਛੋੜ ਦਿਵਸ ਤੇ ਪੜੇ ਜਾਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਸ਼ਬਦਾਂ ਦਾ ਸੰਗ੍ਰਹਿ ਮਰਿਆਦਾ ਸਹਿਤ)

Title: Sri Diwali Path Mahatam
Gurmukhi: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਪਾਠ ਮਹਾਤਮ (ਮਰਿਆਦਾ ਸਹਿਤ) – ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੰਗਲਾਚਰਨ ਜੀ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੁਖਿਵਾਕ ਪਾਤਿਸਾਹੀ ੧੦

Title: Sarbloh Granth Manglacharan – Ustat Sri Maya Lachhmi Ji ki
Gurmukhi: ਉਸਤਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮਾਯਾ ਲਛਮੀ ਜੀ ਕੀ (ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੰਗਲਾਚਰਨ)
Authors: Attributed to Guru Gobind Singh (Sri Mukhvak Patshahi 10)

Title: Sampooran Sri Sarbloh Granth Sahib Ji
Gurmukhi: ਸੰਪੂਰਨ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਸਰਬਲੋਹ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ – ਪੋਥੀ ਭਾਗ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਤੇ ਦੂਜਾ – ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੁਖ ਵਾਕ ਪਾ: ੧੦
Authors: Attributed to Guru Gobind Singh (as printed)

Title: Sri Bhavani Ustat
Gurmukhi: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਭਵਾਨੀ ਉਸਤਤਿ + ੩. ਸਰਬ ਲੋਹ ਕਵਚ
Authors: Attributed to Guru Gobind Singh (Sri Mukhvak Patshahi 10)

Title: Sahaj Paath Maryada of Sri Sarbloh Prakash Granth Sahib
Gurmukhi: ਸ੍ਰੀ ਸਹਿਜ ਪਾਠ ਮਰਿਆਦਾ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਮੁਖਵਾਕ ਪਾਤਸ਼ਾਹੀ ੧੦ – ਸ੍ਰੀ ਸਰਬਲੋਹ ਪ੍ਰਕਾਸ਼ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਜੀ
Authors: Sangreh karta: Giani Gurvinder Singh Ji Nangli

Title: Lesson 1
Authors: unknown (no byline; probably the same English translation project as 'The Path to Learning Gurbani Pronunciation')

Title: Lesson 2
Authors: unknown (no byline; same series as Lesson 1)

Title: The Path to Learning Gurbānī Pronunciation
Authors: Vidiā Gurū Gianī Gurwinder Singh Nangalī, Ustād Gurmat Vidiālā, Chabbā, Nangalī

Title: Singh Sagar
Known from: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, 'Singh Sagar' (Rattan Singh Jaggi)
Notes: Braj verse life of Guru Gobind Singh in 14 tarangs, written at Patiala (1884 Bk / 1827); sequel to the author's Gur Kirat Prakash. EoS reports two MSS (one at Motibagh Palace) and a 1986 Punjabi University edition.

Title: Gur Kirat Prakash
Known from: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, 'Gur Kirat Prakash' (Piara Singh Padam)
Notes: Braj verse lives of the first nine Gurus in ten hulas, completed 1891 Bk / 1834 at the Patiala court. EoS reports MSS at Punjab State Archives (No. 682) and Punjabi University, and a 1986 Punjabi University edition.

Title: Bansavalinama Dasan Patshahian Ka
Known from: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, 'Bansavalinama Dasan Patshahian Ka' (Rattan Singh Jaggi)
Notes: Punjabi verse account of the Gurus and after, 2,564 stanzas in 14 chapters, completed 1826 Bk / 1769 at Jammu. EoS reports a MS at Khalsa College Amritsar, one lost in 1984 at the Sikh Reference Library, and Jaggi's 1972 edition in Parakh (Panjab University).

Title: Sri Guru Dasam Panchasika
Known from: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism, 'Sri Guru Dasam Panchasika' (Dharam Singh)
Notes: Braj panegyric of the Gurus by a Jind court poet, completed c. 1919 Bk / 1862. EoS: unpublished; only MS at Motibagh Palace, Patiala, MS 148 (29 ff.).

Title: Gurpranali (anonymous, Motibagh MS)
Notes: Anonymous short chronology of the Ten Gurus (births, children, deaths, years of guruship). EoS: unpublished, one MS of six folios in the Motibagh Palace Library, Patiala; no shelfmark given.
